content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.2) — model fails to capture sharp drops or mean reversion.
- Lag in price corrections: model often delays downward adjustments after sentiment shifts to bearish.
- Overshoot after spikes: model overreacts to short-term spikes, especially when sentiment is high, then undercorrects.
- Mean reversion bias: model overestimates continuation of trends, especially in 30-day horizon, ignoring recent volatility.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.3, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period; if sentiment < 0.2, increase by 2–5% to account for underreaction.
